answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: every identity posts a small bond, and its influence grows only through sustained useful work, like a lotus that must root before it blooms. Reputation fades without fresh contributions, so a sock-puppet farm faces the umber reality of re-earning standing it cannot stockpile. To cross the ridge between newcomer and trusted member, accounts must also pass random peer audits. Correlated failures reveal linked fakes and slash their bonds. Creating identities stays cheap, but making each one influential costs real, ongoing effort.
